citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 174; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Le général Reynier apprenant que le gros de l'armée royale l'attendait dans un camp retranché à Campo Tenese, plaine haute entourée de montagnes, qui a deux étroites vallées pour entrée et pour issue, se mit en mouvement le 9 à la pointe du jour, fit serrer les deux dernières colonnes sur la première, et après une courte halte à Rotonda, délogea une centaine de chevaux napolitains venus en reconnaissance.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: on the 9th Reynier moved at daybreak, closed the following columns, halted at Rotonda and dislodged Neapolitan reconnaissance horse; this reports a local displacement, not the opening positions of every component.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 174; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Il s'engagea ensuite dans le défilé de San Martino en faisant explorer par des flanqueurs les montagnes qui le bordent. Les avant-postes ennemis furent repoussés par nos éclaireurs, et dès que la tête de colonne commença à déboucher, il détacha plusieurs compagnies de voltigeurs sur les montagnes à droite et à gauche de la plaine de Campo Tenese.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: he next entered the San Martino defile; scouts repulsed enemy outposts before companies were detached onto the mountains as the column head emerged.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 174; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Le général Damas avait militairement choisi sa position; son corps de bataille occupait la plaine sur deux lignes dont les ailes s'appuyaient aux hauteurs où

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Damas had chosen his position and his battle body occupied the plain in two lines, with wings resting on heights; the sentence continues on p.175.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 175; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: étaient placés d'équerre plusieurs bataillons. Trois redoutes, armées chacune de deux ou trois pièces de gros calibre, couvraient le centre.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: battalions occupied the heights at right angles and three armed redoubts covered the centre. This describes the position without dating every unit to the earlier reconnaissance contact.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 175; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Cependant il fallait presser l'attaque : un bataillon du 42e est envoyé sur les hauteurs de gauche pour appuyer les voltigeurs du 1er léger vivement engagés; l'avant-garde se forme en face des redoutes, la division Verdier en seconde ligne, mais avec lenteur, l'exiguïté du défilé obligeant souvent à marcher par file simple. Reynier, apprenant que les hauteurs viennent d'être balayées, que deux bataillons, chargés de leur défense, sont en fuite, et qu'ainsi la droite de l'ennemi est débordée, ordonne au général Compère de faire battre la charge et de marcher la baïonnette en avant, et à la division Verdier de soutenir son mouvement.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: the 42nd battalion supports already-engaged light troops; the advance guard forms before the redoubts, Verdier follows slowly through the defile, then a charge is ordered. Narrative order is not a synchronized roster.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 176; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: La brigade de chasseurs à cheval du général Franceschi, retenue dans le défilé de San Martino, ne put prendre part à l'action et tomber sur l'ennemi au moment où il prit la fuite; elle bivouaqua à Campo Tenese, y recueillit les prisonniers, et fournit un détachement pour les escorter jusqu'à Salerne.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Franceschi’s cavalry was held in the defile and could not participate, then bivouacked at Campo Tenese and handled prisoners. Nonparticipation does not establish unavailability at the earlier contact.

citation.locator: Memoirs of the Comte Roger de Damas (1913), printed p. 395; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: It became necessary for my right wing to retire without delay; and the position of Campo Tenese, which I had fortified and furnished with artillery, I determined to use in the way I have already described, to check the enemy with my left and effect a junction of the two wings. This was a very good position: it could only be turned by crossing almost inaccessible mountains, for the defence of which we were prepared. It was here that the enemy attacked me at two o'clock in the afternoon of the 9th March,

passages.interpretation_en: Damas distinguishes withdrawal of his right wing and a junction objective from the attack on his Campo Tenese position, reported at two o’clock on 9 March. That clock does not date Koch’s earlier outpost/reconnaissance encounters.

citation.locator: Memoirs of the Comte Roger de Damas (1913), printed p. 396; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Finally all the recruits who were occupying the curtains and redoubts turned tail and fled: the troops who were defending the hill on the right followed their example, and the enemy was then able to turn the rest of the force.

passages.interpretation_en: Damas places recruits in curtains/redoubts and troops on the right hill during the action; it does not give a complete roster at the earlier approach contact.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 240; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: In consequence of the observations made this evening, an order was issued for the march of the troops at daylight on the morning of the 4th, with the declared purpose of attacking the enemy's camp.

passages.interpretation_en: Bunbury explicitly dates the intended attack march to daylight on the 4th; an order is not hostile contact.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 240; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Four companies of Watteville's regiment under that good Swiss officer, Major Fischer, with a detachment of artillerymen, and three out of our six fieldpieces, were left to secure the tower and our entrenchments on the beach.

passages.interpretation_en: Watteville companies, artillerymen and field pieces were left at the tower/beach entrenchments, separately from the marching field force.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 241; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: march, with 4795 rank and file, a great majority of whom had never seen an enemy. The 27th was the only battalion of old soldiers: the flank companies of the 20th, 27th, 35th, and 61st also were hard-biting fellows of long standing;

passages.interpretation_en: The marching number is rank and file; the light/flank companies of the 20th are part of this description. It is not an officers-included all-arms return.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 241; matched to registered page image
citation.quote:
Our course, therefore, ran along the shingly shore and some marshy pastures which bordered it: our progress was slow and there was a considerable difficulty in bringing on even our three field guns.

The Calabrian sun arose in its full strength of July, and our men began to be jaded* before they reached the open ground near the mouth of the Lamato. A detachment of the enemy's light cavalry retired as we drew near; and just as our two columns opened into the lower part of the plain of Maida, we descried the French army filing by its right from the position in which it had bivouacked on the high ground and descending into the upper portion of the same plain.

passages.interpretation_en: The march passes shore and marsh, cavalry retires as the columns approach, and French troops descend into the upper plain. Withdrawal alone does not prove hostile contact.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 242; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: The shallow stream of the Lamato, bordered with thickets, ran upon our right; the plain, gradually widening, was in our front; and on the left there extended broken and irregular patches of coarse grass and bushes and coppicewood.

passages.interpretation_en: The Lamato, thickets, widening plain and coppice describe the local field area, not a measured polygon.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 243; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: advance was made in an échelon of brigades, the right, Kempt's* Light Infantry, taking the lead. Next came Acland's brigade; then Cole's; and Oswald with his thirteen companies (58th and Watteville's) followed in rear of the centre as a reserve.

passages.interpretation_en: Bunbury names the brigade order and Oswald’s reserve behind the centre. A reserve is not excluded merely because its later engagement differs; exact placement at the first shot is not timed here.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 243; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: For some time we saw nothing of the enemy, excepting their cavalry, which manœuvred across our front, raising a great dust which served to screen their infantry, and three pieces of horse-artillery whose fire did little injury, and was returned with interest by our own three guns under Lieut.-Colonel Lemoine and Captain Pym.

passages.interpretation_en: French horse artillery fires and British guns reply before the narrated riverside infantry skirmish and main clash. Gun numbers do not supply crew headcounts.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 243; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: As our right drew nigh to the steep and woody bank on the left side of the Lamato, where the French huts were standing, Colonel Kempt detached the Corsican Rangers across the stream to scour the thickets and secure him from ambuscades on his flank, sending at the same time the light company of the 20th as a support. Scarcely had the Corsicans entered the wood when they were met by a brisk fire, followed by the headlong charge of about 200 French, and were driven in such confusion upon the 20th that this company was hard put to it to keep its ground; its Captain, McLean, was killed, and if the men had not been of sterling stuff the company must have been broken. The fire for some minutes was very sharp, and the parties were close to each other; but Kempt instantly detached Major Robertson across the stream with the flankers of the 35th, and matters were speedily righted.

passages.interpretation_en: The Corsican Rangers cross with the 20th light company in support; firing and a French charge follow, and 35th flankers are sent across. This is distinct from Ross’s body later reported approaching.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 244; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: While this skirmish was going on, our little army was advancing very gradually up the plain, but as yet nothing was distinguishable beyond the thick dust of the French cavalry, who made repeated feints of charging on one or other of our brigades. The extreme heat of the morning also produced a sort of mirage in the low grounds, which served further to perplex our sight, and we still inclined to the belief that Reynier was retiring up the valley, and covering his march by the display of his horsemen, and by the little ambuscade on the hill. Suddenly, however, the enemy's cavalry moved rapidly away beyond the front of our extreme left; and as their dust cleared off, we saw the French infantry formed for attack and marching rapidly upon us. We saw at the same time that the enemy outnumbered us considerably; their formation as well as ours was oblique, the enemy's left and our right being each in advance. Their 1r Legère (three battalions) led on by General Compère, and supported by a regiment of Poles, advanced in line upon the brigade of British Light Infantry; which likewise continued to move onward. A crashing fire of musquetry soon opened on both sides,

passages.interpretation_en: The main columns advance while the skirmish occurs; the main infantry fire follows. The main clash is not the earliest fire described by Bunbury.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 246; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: one of my assistants came galloping to me from the beach, with the welcome tidings that the 20th Regiment had landed, and was coming through the brushwood at double quick time.

passages.interpretation_en: During the continuing fight, Bunbury receives news that the 20th has landed and is approaching through the brushwood. This later report gives no landing clock or opening availability; do not merge it with the 20th light company.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 253; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Including the Poles at Monteleone and other places, but exclusive of the troops left at Scilla and Reggio, Reynier had under his command 7300 men; and I believe he had in the action about 6300, including nearly 300 cavalry, an arm in which we were entirely deficient.

passages.interpretation_en: A broader command total includes Monteleone and other places while excluding Scilla/Reggio; a separate belief concerns actual action participants. Neither is automatically the opening local target.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 189; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: A peine Reynier en eut-il été informé qu'il rassembla ses troupes et marcha avec tant de diligence que sa division, forte de 4,500 hommes d'infanterie, de 300 chasseurs à cheval et d'une batterie d'artillerie légère, passa la nuit du 3 au 4 dans le bois de Fondaco del Fico, d'où elle déboucha le 5 dans la plaine, par la route tracée entre le pied des hauteurs de Maida et la rive gauche du Lamato.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: infantry, cavalry and a light-artillery battery spent the night of the 3rd–4th in the wood, then debouched on the 5th. The printed 5th conflicts with Bunbury’s 4th; artillery personnel and state continuity are unresolved.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 238; matched to registered page image (OCR spelling retained)
citation.quote: His advanced people had proceeded but a little way, when they were assailed by a brisk fire from the thickets,

passages.interpretation_en: Earlier expedition context: Bunbury describes fire during the landing sequence. The new local field-engagement scenario explicitly separates this earlier episode; the landing and whole expedition are not automatically the field opening.

citation.locator: Bunbury, Narratives (1854), printed p. 238; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: In the course of the next morning, July 1st, all the troops were landed, with six guns, and ten mountain pieces which were to be carried on the backs of mules.

passages.interpretation_en: The next morning is labelled July 1st. This dates the earlier landing narrative relatively without inventing an exact timestamp for its skirmish.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 196; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Ces officiers se présentèrent aussitôt en parlementaires, mais soit à cause de l'heure avancée, soit défiance ou inexpérience de la part de la garnison, ils furent reçus à coups de fusil, et le chef d'escadron Lamy tomba victime de cette erreur.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: officers presenting themselves as parlementaires were met by rifle shots and Lamy was killed. The inspected page does not supply a complete event date; this is contact even though the narrator calls it an error.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 196; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Le gouverneur consentit au rendez-vous, qui fut fixé pour le 15 chez le consul ottoman, dans le faubourg; mais sous prétexte d'une indisposition, il s'y fit représenter par son premier aide de camp. Dans cette entrevue, l'on convint qu'il y aurait armistice jusqu'à l'arrivée de nouvelles instructions de la cour de Palerme, et que la ligne d'investissement couperait le faubourg par moitié et s'étendrait de là, parallèlement à la place, jusqu'à la plage de Sérapis. Le prince de Hesse accepta ce tracé à condition que les Français ne mettraient pas de poste dans le faubourg.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: the negotiated investment line divides the faubourg and runs parallel to the place to the Sérapis beach; Hesse objects to French posts in the faubourg. It is a proposed/contested line, not proof of a complete occupied roster.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 196; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Tout fut rompu; le gouverneur irrité de sa roideur fit bombarder la maison où il logeait,

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: after the breakdown, the governor bombarded Lacour’s lodging. The act is separate from the later formal siege-battery opening.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 205; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Le 4 mars au soir donc, ainsi qu'il avait été résolu, on commence la batterie de mortiers n° 1 dans le jardin des Augustins ou Recollets à couvert de la place par les murs de clôture (voy. note n° VII); l'emplacement de la batterie de canons n° 1, destinée à forcer les bâtiments mouillés dans le port à gagner le large, est à l'entrée du faubourg au pont de Celagno. Comme cette dernière n'était vue de la place que par 2 pièces de la batterie Santa Maria à une distance de plus de 2,500 mètres, on ne lui fit point d'abord d'épaulement pour ne pas donner l'éveil à l'ennemi; dans la suite on la masqua par un léger parapet.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: on the evening of 4 March a mortar battery was begun; the passage describes construction and emplacement, not the first firing event.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 233; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Le corps de siége se composait à cette époque de 8,500 hommes de toutes armes devant la place, de 800 sur le Garigliano et de 900 répartis dans les différents postes, depuis le camp jusqu'à Terracine; la force de la garnison s'élevait, d'après le rapport des déserteurs, à environ 6,200 hommes.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: at this epoch troops before the place, on the Garigliano and in posts to Terracina are separately stated; the garrison figure is a deserter report. This is the July preparation state, not the initial encounter.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 233; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: On espérait pouvoir commencer le feu le 6 au matin, mais les accidents de la veille le firent ajourner au lendemain. Dans la journée on continua l'armement et l'approvisionnement des batteries sous un feu très-vif; quelques bâtiments ennemis quittent le mouillage. Le maréchal Massena crut devoir faire une dernière sommation avant de commencer le feu, mais elle resta sans effet.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: the planned opening on the 6th is postponed to the next day while preparations continue under very lively fire. Garrison fire already exists before that battery opening.

citation.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), printed p. 30; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Al giorno delle prime offese, 7 luglio, montavano gli assediati intorno a settemila, metà degli assediatori; bordeggiavano in giro alla fortezza o stavano ancorati nel porto quattro vascelli inglesi, sei fregate, trenta cannoniere o bombarde, alcune navi da trasporto.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Colletta calls 7 July the first offenses and describes besieged, besiegers and ships. This wording is retained as a phase account; it does not erase the earlier fire in Koch or convert ship crews into land troops.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 280; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Tranquille sur ce point, Verdier, conformément aux ordres du maréchal, partit de Cosenza le 3 décembre pour réduire Amantea, à la tête de 1,300 hommes, 2 obusiers et 2 pièces de montagne.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Verdier departed Cosenza on 3 December for Amantea with a stated force and guns, before the frozen 18 December interval.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 280; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Cette ville, bâtie sur un roc près de la mer, à 30 kilomètres sud-ouest de Cosenza, a une enceinte de forme à peu près carrée, abritée de trois côtés par l'escarpement des rochers sur lesquels elle s'appuie, et fermée par un vieux front bastionné sur le 4e; elle était à peine à l'abri d'un coup de main, mais l'insurrection lui avait donné de l'importance, parce qu'on pouvait y remonter en barques, de la mer; elle était armée de 4 à 5 pièces de canon et défendue par des troupes régulières, quelques centaines d'insurgés et ses habitants, le tout aux ordres du colonel Mirabelli, natif d'Amantea, qui jouissait d'une grande considération dans le canton.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: the rock/sea and bastioned front define approaches; regulars, insurgents and inhabitants defend under Mirabelli. No complete assigned-combatant roster or later opening state is established.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 281; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: place, Verdier tenta sur le front bastionné une première escalade qui échoua. Une seconde, essayée à quelques jours de là entre les rochers qui font face à la mer, pendant qu'on attaquait de vive force le front bastionné, resta également sans succès. Ces deux échecs, la consommation des vivres et des munitions, et de plus l'inquiétude que donnèrent à Verdier 3,000 insurgés qui s'étaient établis entre Lagonegro et Amantea, le déterminèrent à se retirer le 8 décembre,

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: failed escalades and other pressures led to withdrawal on 8 December; that attempt is separate from the later investment.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 281; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: En exécution de ses ordres, un corps de 1,200 hommes conduits par le colonel Huard, remplissant les

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: a body under Huard begins the clause; p.282 continues it with the investment on the 18th. The page break must not detach the force from its event.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 282; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: fonctions de général de brigade, forma l'investissement de la forteresse le 18.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Huard formed the investment of the fortress on the 18th. Investment is an operational marker, not proof of hostile fire at that instant.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 282; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Verdier se mit en mouvement le 22 avec 2,500 hommes et 6 bouches à feu; il fut suivi le lendemain par une colonne de 1,000 hommes qu'amenait le général Reynier, lequel dirigea toutes les opérations du siége.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Verdier sets out on the 22nd and the next day Reynier follows with another column. These are departures, not arrivals or proof of concurrent unchanged forces at the investment.

citation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V (1850), printed p. 282; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: On ouvrit un boyau de tranchée à 260 mètres de la place, et on le poussa à 40 mètres de la capitale du bastion de droite où l'on établit une batterie de 6 pièces qui firent écrouler l'escarpe, après 48 heures de feu. Plusieurs assauts ayant été repoussés, il fallut entrer en galerie, et ce ne fut que le 6 février, après 33 jours de siége, que la place capitula.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: trench/battery work, fire, failed assaults and mining precede capitulation on 6 February after 33 siege days. Do not reverse-engineer a precise formal opening date from the duration.

citation.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), printed p. 31; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Amantea è città di Calabria di duemilacinquecento abitatori, fondata quasi su la marina del Tirreno, sopra un gran sasso, già scoglio; la chiudono da tre lati le rupi, e dal quarto un vecchio muro fra due deboli bastioni; pochi soldati la guardavano e molti

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Amantea’s town inhabitants and terrain are described, followed by few soldiers and many other defenders in a sentence continued on p.32. Inhabitants are not a complete combatant count.

citation.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), printed p. 32; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Il generale Verdier, con tremila duecento soldati, artiglierie ed attrezzi, andò ad assaltarla; e quindi, cinta quella fronte del castello che è verso la campagna, alzata una batteria di cannoni e di obici, agli albòri del giorno, per segno convenuto, avanzarono a corsa con le scale i soldati più prodi; ma la forza del luogo ed il valore del presidio li respinse, sicchè scemati ritornarono ai campi.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: Verdier’s stated body assaults after landward encirclement and battery preparation; a dawn escalade is repulsed. The dawn assault has no stated date; only the subsequent night assault is explicitly placed in December.

citation.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), printed p. 32; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: In una notte lunga e fosca del dicembre, piccolo drappello di sette uomini de'quali primo il più destro, rampicandosi fra'sassi che separano dal mare la città, tanto oltre avanzò che sentiva il parlare delle ascolte nemiche, mentre colonna più numerosa con funi e scale tacitamente seguiva le segnate tracce, ed altre schiere gridando e sparando attaccavano il muro bastionato per divertire i difensori dal vero assalto. Ma per voce infantile che dalla fronte di mare grida i Francesi, accorrono le guardie, tirano sassi ed archibugiate verso il luogo che il fanciullo indicava; è colpito un de'sette e muore, altri della colonna maggiore sono feriti; ma nessuno si lagna per non discoprire la impresa. Si rassicurava per quel silenzio il presidio, scemavano i colpi, udivasi un Calabrese rimprocciare il fanciullo dell'affermare ostinato di aver visto e inteso i nemici, quando un obice del campo scoppiò in aria, e con la luce palesò gli assalitori. Mille offese ad un punto partirono da'vicini ripari, molti dei Francesi furono morti, si arrestarono gli altri e si raccolsero nei campi. Il generale, poi che vidde non bastare le sorprese, non gl'inganni, non le forze, levato l'assedio, ritornò doglioso ed assetato di vendetta in Cosenza.

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: a December night assault, defensive fire and subsequent lifting of the siege are described. The month alone does not place that night attack before 18 December or independently identify it with Koch’s earlier attempt.

citation.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), printed p. 32; matched to registered page image
citation.quote: Ma finito il dicembre, egli, più forte, meglio provvisto di macchine, ritornò agli assalti, conducendo dalle sue parti il colonnello Amato, pur cittadino di Amantea, congiunto è da fanciullezza compagno ed amico al Mirabelli;

passages.interpretation_en: Primary English rendering: after December Verdier returns stronger and better equipped. There is no complete personnel figure, first-contact date or reconciliation with Koch’s phases.

events.assertion_en: Local reconnaissance horse forcibly displaced; first explicit local hostile act in this Koch sequence.
Scouts repulse outposts in the San Martino approach.
Engagement on heights and attack on the main position; following line restricted in the defile.
Damas’s reported attack on his fortified Campo Tenese position; no synchronized link to Koch’s reconnaissance contact.
Cavalry bivouacs at Campo Tenese after the action; the cited passage separately describes its nonparticipation.

events.date_label: earlier landing sequence; before the next morning labelled July 1st, Bunbury
events.assertion_en: Landing-context skirmish; outside the separately proposed field-engagement scope.
Field force ordered to march while a tower guard is left behind.
Columns approach the plain and cavalry retires; no explicit fire in this passage.
Artillery exchange; earliest explicit local fire in this source sequence.
Riverside skirmish involving Corsicans, 20th light company and supporting flankers.
Main infantry fire follows the skirmish’s onset.
Report that Ross’s 20th has landed and is approaching; exact landing/first availability time unknown.

events.date_label: 5 July advance after night of 3rd–4th, Koch
events.assertion_en: French division advances; source date alternative retained without correction.

events.date_label: retrospective command/action comparison, Bunbury; state date unstated
events.assertion_en: Broader command and action-participation populations, including distant detachments, have different scopes.

membership_cases.label: French force performing the narrated reconnaissance displacement
membership_cases.note: Local actors only; the passage does not identify a complete detachment roster or total.

membership_cases.label: Following lines and height detachments
membership_cases.note: Positions during the developing attack do not establish every component’s place at the earlier displacement.

membership_cases.label: Franceschi cavalry
membership_cases.note: Retained in the defile/nonparticipating is not proof of opening absence or unavailability.

membership_cases.label: Neapolitan reconnaissance horse
membership_cases.note: This local party is present at the displacement; identity of a complete force remains unestablished.

membership_cases.label: Redoubt/height defenders and main lines
membership_cases.note: Sources place defenders at the main action, without a complete roster synchronized to the earlier approach contact.

membership_cases.label: Separate right wing intended for junction
membership_cases.note: An intended junction/retreat does not put this wing into the local opening force.

membership_cases.label: French firing horse artillery
membership_cases.note: At least the operating combat component is local at the exchange; no crew total or whole force follows.

membership_cases.label: Koch’s night-of-3rd–4th division components
membership_cases.note: No cross-account date correction or continuity of all components to Bunbury’s earliest fire is inferred.

membership_cases.label: Distant detachments at Monteleone/other garrisons
membership_cases.note: Exclude these distant components by the local-area rule; do not exclude all of the overlapping broader command total or subtract it from actual participants.

membership_cases.label: British replying guns and operating combat component
membership_cases.note: Replying batteries are local at the contact event; guns are not a crew headcount.

membership_cases.label: Marching brigades and Oswald reserve
membership_cases.note: The reserve is not excluded for its role; successive emergence from marsh/wood leaves its exact opening position unresolved.

membership_cases.label: Watteville/tower guards and detached artillerymen
membership_cases.note: Outside the declared field corridor even though relevant to the expedition’s security.

membership_cases.label: 20th light company with Kempt
membership_cases.note: The skirmish proves local participation after the earlier artillery episode; it alone gives no first-shot roster. Keep it separate from Ross’s body.

membership_cases.label: Ross’s 20th body reported approaching
membership_cases.note: Later news/approach is not an exact landing time and does not establish opening availability or a late-arrival clock. No opening inclusion is made.

membership_cases.label: Marching rank-and-file population
membership_cases.note: The partial personnel basis cannot be converted into an officers-included all-arms total; component location/continuity to first fire is not complete.

membership_cases.label: Initial local brigade/negotiating party
membership_cases.note: A subsequent negotiation/line account does not supply complete strength or positions before the initial rifle shots.

membership_cases.label: Troops before the place at the July preparation epoch
membership_cases.note: A July 5th–6th epoch observation does not prove unchanged personnel at the formal opening, still less at the earlier initial encounter.

membership_cases.label: Garigliano detached body
membership_cases.note: Excluded by the declared local-area rule, not because it was irrelevant to the wider siege.

membership_cases.label: Camp-to-Terracina posts
membership_cases.note: A group spanning camp to Terracina cannot all be excluded or included as local; a split/location roster is absent.

membership_cases.label: Garrison riflemen at the parlementaire encounter
membership_cases.note: Source places the firing combat component locally; complete date, operation link and opening garrison population remain unresolved.

membership_cases.label: Besieged/garrison estimates at the July phase
membership_cases.note: The accounts supply different bases/hearsay; no complete assigned-combatant roster or backcast to initial contact.

membership_cases.label: Naval/transport crews remaining afloat
membership_cases.note: Outside the land target. Any disembarked combat personnel need separate evidence; ships are not added as people.

membership_cases.label: Huard’s investing body
membership_cases.note: Local component at an investment marker only; the marker does not establish hostile contact or a complete all-arms total.

membership_cases.label: Verdier column departing later
membership_cases.note: A column only setting out on the 22nd is not a simultaneous opening component at the explicit 18th investment scenario. Arrival remains unknown.

membership_cases.label: Reynier column following Verdier next day
membership_cases.note: Following the later departure is incompatible with presence as this intact column at the 18th marker; no exact arrival time follows.

membership_cases.label: Earlier attempt’s personnel
membership_cases.note: An earlier departure/withdrawal count does not establish who later rejoined the investment; do not confuse exclusion of an old observation with proof every old individual was absent.

membership_cases.label: Colletta initial assault body
membership_cases.note: The initial dawn assault is undated; the later night is dated only to December. Alignment to Koch/frozen interval remains unresolved; no opening quantity selected.

membership_cases.label: All later siege columns together
membership_cases.note: Later activity does not prove concurrent unchanged/disjoint column strengths or complete coverage. The arithmetic sum remains a blocked later-phase proposal.

membership_cases.label: Entire town population
membership_cases.note: The inhabitants include people not established as defenders. Exclude the aggregate population basis; assigned armed inhabitants could qualify with separate evidence.

membership_cases.label: Regulars, insurgents and assigned armed inhabitants
membership_cases.note: Descriptions of the earlier defense and town do not provide an opening combat-assignment roster at a defined contact. No whole-town substitution.
